products.name: Automation Cloud Administration and Test Cloud Administration

Automation Cloud Administration and Test.summary: Administration adds broader AI Trust Layer visibility and impact analysis, consumables visibility improvements, and a notification email discontinuation. It also introduces BYO-model support for a UI Automation semantic activity and includes required model migration and retirement updates.
Automation Cloud Administration and Test.overall_analysis: These changes strengthen administrative oversight of AI model usage, dependencies, and consumption while signaling ongoing model lifecycle management responsibilities. They also reduce reliance on legacy notifications and require admins to adapt to provider model replacements and retirements.

changes.name: Model hub generally available
changes.summary: Model hub in the AI Trust Layer is now generally available. It gives administrators a central view of the provider, model, routing region, and lifecycle status behind each product feature, for every tenant in the organization. Document Understanding models now also appear in Model hub.
changes.analysis: This likely improves governance and transparency for AI feature dependencies across tenants, helping administrators understand what models are in use and where.
changes.impact: Organization administrators and teams overseeing AI usage across Automation Cloud and Test Cloud tenants; includes visibility into Document Understanding models.

changes.name: Model impact preview tab
changes.summary: Model impact, a new tenant-level Model hub tab, is available in preview. It shows which products, features, and processes depend on each model, how often they call it, and when they last used it.
changes.analysis: This likely helps tenants assess operational dependence on specific models and evaluate risk before changing or retiring model configurations.
changes.impact: Tenant administrators managing model usage, dependency tracking, and change planning.

changes.name: BYO LLM for Close Popup semantic activity
changes.summary: You can now power the Close Popup semantic activity in UI Automation with your own LLM subscription.
changes.analysis: This likely gives customers more control over model sourcing, compliance, and cost for this semantic automation capability.
changes.impact: Administrators and automation teams using UI Automation and bring-your-own-model configurations.

changes.name: Kimi K2.7 Code replaced by Kimi K3
changes.summary: Kimi K2.7 Code is replaced with Kimi K3. Bring-your-own-model configurations that reference Kimi K2.7 Code must be updated to Kimi K3, or they fall back to UiPath-managed models.
changes.analysis: This is a model lifecycle update that requires configuration maintenance to preserve intended BYO-model behavior.
changes.impact: Customers with bring-your-own-model configurations referencing Kimi K2.7 Code.

changes.name: Azure OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock model retirements announced
changes.summary: Azure OpenAI retires gpt-4o-2024-05-13 on September 30, 2026, and Amazon Bedrock retires anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-20250514-v1:0 on October 13, 2026.
changes.analysis: The announcement gives customers time to prepare for provider-side model retirements that may affect dependent features or configurations.
changes.impact: Administrators and teams relying on those specific provider models.

changes.name: Consumables Overview button
changes.summary: Each unit card on the Consumables tab now has an Overview button that shows consumption charts without opening the full Consumables Center dashboard.
changes.analysis: This likely streamlines quick consumption checks and reduces navigation overhead for administrators monitoring usage.
changes.impact: Administrators reviewing consumables usage.

changes.name: Daily notification summary email discontinued
changes.summary: The daily notification summary email is discontinued starting November 1, 2026. Digest emails and notification subscriptions are not affected.
changes.analysis: This simplifies the notification model while preserving other notification mechanisms, but users relying on the daily summary must adjust.
changes.impact: Users and administrators who rely on daily notification summary emails.

Action Center.summary: Action Center makes human-in-the-loop task authoring via coding agent generally available and improves Validation Station compact view usability with collapsible field groups. The changes focus on task integration and reviewer efficiency.
Action Center.overall_analysis: The release strengthens both automation design and validation workflows by making human review steps easier to add and making dense validation interfaces easier to navigate.

changes.name: Human-in-the-loop tasks via coding agent generally available
changes.summary: Adding human-in-the-loop tasks to an automation with a coding agent is now generally available, through the `uipath-human-in-the-loop` skill.
changes.analysis: This likely makes it easier to include human review and decision points when building automations through coding-agent-assisted development.
changes.impact: Developers and automation builders using coding agents to create automations with Action Center tasks.

changes.name: Collapsible field groups in Validation Station compact view
changes.summary: Field groups in the compact view of the Validation Station can now be collapsed, per group or per instance.
changes.analysis: This likely improves usability and focus for validators working with many grouped fields or repeated instances.
changes.impact: Users performing document or data validation in Validation Station.

Agents.summary: Agents expands general availability for coding-agent-based agent development and Data Fabric entity context, while introducing preview support for advanced agents and Autopilot Agent in Studio Web. The release broadens both agent-building methods and runtime options.
Agents.overall_analysis: These updates indicate a significant maturation of the agent platform, with more production-ready development paths and new preview capabilities for complex, long-running workloads.

changes.name: Low-code and coded agents via coding agent generally available
changes.summary: Building low-code and coded agents with a coding agent is now generally available, through the `uipath-agents` skill.
changes.analysis: This likely lowers development effort and standardizes agent creation workflows through assisted development.
changes.impact: Developers and automation teams building agents in low-code or coded styles.

changes.name: Data Fabric entities as structured agent context generally available
changes.summary: Using Data Fabric entities as structured agent context is now generally available.
changes.analysis: This likely improves how agents consume structured business data, enabling more reliable context injection.
changes.impact: Teams building agents that use Data Fabric entities for context.

changes.name: Advanced agents preview
changes.summary: Advanced agents are available in preview. They run on an alternative harness for long-running, document-heavy work, with a file workspace, sub-agents, and programmatic tool calls.
changes.analysis: This expands the kinds of workloads agents can handle, especially more complex or longer-running tasks involving documents and orchestration of tools or sub-agents.
changes.impact: Developers exploring more capable agent architectures for complex workloads.

changes.name: Autopilot Agent preview in Studio Web
changes.summary: Autopilot Agent, a coding agent built into Studio Web, is available in preview and is now the default Autopilot experience for agents. You can switch back to classic Autopilot.
changes.analysis: This likely updates the default assisted-development experience for agents while keeping a fallback path for users not ready to switch.
changes.impact: Studio Web users building agents with Autopilot.

Apps.summary: Apps adds generally available coding-agent support for coded web apps and Action apps, and extends the Apps API with deployed app deletion. The updates improve both app development and lifecycle management.
Apps.overall_analysis: The changes continue the platform's shift toward coding-agent-assisted development while filling an API management gap for deployed applications.

changes.name: Coded web apps and Action apps via coding agent generally available
changes.summary: Building coded web apps and Action apps with a coding agent is now generally available, through the `uipath-coded-apps` skill.
changes.analysis: This likely accelerates app development and broadens coding-agent support across app types.
changes.impact: Developers building coded web apps or Action apps.

changes.name: Apps API supports deleting deployed apps
changes.summary: The Apps API now supports deleting a deployed app.
changes.analysis: This likely improves deployment lifecycle automation and cleanup through API-based administration.
changes.impact: Developers and administrators managing deployed apps through the Apps API.

Automation Cloud Robots.summary: Automation Cloud Robots has a documentation-only update: relevant documentation moved from the Orchestrator guide to the Robot guide. This affects where users find product guidance rather than product behavior.
Automation Cloud Robots.overall_analysis: The significance is organizational and discoverability-focused, helping align documentation with product ownership and usage patterns.

changes.name: Documentation moved to Robot guide
changes.summary: The Cloud Robots, Elastic Robot Orchestration, and Automation Suite Robots documentation for Automation Cloud moved from the Orchestrator guide to the Robot guide.
changes.analysis: This likely improves documentation structure and makes robot-related guidance easier to find in a more appropriate location.
changes.impact: Users and administrators looking for Automation Cloud Robots documentation.

Automation Hub.summary: Automation Hub improves integration with UiPath Cartographer and adds process-model-linked automation benefit rollups and visual enhancements. The changes strengthen idea creation and business process alignment.
Automation Hub.overall_analysis: These updates make it easier to connect discovery artifacts and process models with automation opportunities, improving traceability and value tracking.

changes.name: Cartographer documents create idea and attach files in one step
changes.summary: Process Design Documents and Solution Design Documents published from UiPath Cartographer now create the automation idea and attach both documents in one step.
changes.analysis: This likely reduces manual setup and preserves documentation context when moving from discovery into automation ideation.
changes.impact: Users publishing process and solution design documents from UiPath Cartographer into Automation Hub.

changes.name: Link automation to process step with rolled-up benefits
changes.summary: You can now link an automation to a step of a business process model and roll its estimated benefit up to the parent process. Three rolled-up benefit columns are available in Workspace, and process model nodes can have a background color.
changes.analysis: This likely improves process-level value analysis and visual organization for business process modeling and automation planning.
changes.impact: Process owners, analysts, and Automation Hub users tracking benefits across business process models.

Automation Ops.summary: Automation Ops introduces public preview coding-agent support for governance policy authoring and CI/CD pipeline management. This expands assisted administration and delivery workflow capabilities.
Automation Ops.overall_analysis: The release suggests a move toward agent-assisted platform governance and DevOps operations, which could reduce manual effort for policy and pipeline management.

changes.name: Coding-agent support for governance and CI/CD in public preview
changes.summary: You can now author governance policies and manage continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines from a coding agent, in public preview, through the `uipath-governance` and `uipath-aops` skills.
changes.analysis: This likely helps administrators and DevOps teams automate or accelerate common governance and delivery management tasks using coding agents.
changes.impact: Automation Ops administrators, governance owners, and CI/CD pipeline managers.

Autopilot.summary: Autopilot becomes available as a coding agent in Studio Web across multiple project types in public preview, with file read/edit limitations for some project types. This broadens where Autopilot can assist development.
Autopilot.overall_analysis: The update positions Autopilot as a cross-project coding assistant in Studio Web, extending its reach while making current limitations explicit for certain project types.

changes.name: Studio Web coding-agent support across project types
changes.summary: Autopilot is available as a coding agent in Studio Web, in public preview, across Maestro Flow, Maestro BPMN, Maestro Case, Agent, API workflow, RPA workflow, Coded App, and Function projects. For RPA workflow, Coded App, and Function projects, it reads and edits files only.
changes.analysis: This likely creates a more unified development assistant experience across project types, though capability depth still varies by project.
changes.impact: Studio Web users working across the listed project types.

Data Fabric.summary: Data Fabric is now generally available in Automation Cloud and adds new entity modeling and query behavior changes, including stricter external query requirements and generally available folder-level entities. The release combines maturity milestones with notable behavior constraints.
Data Fabric.overall_analysis: These changes mark Data Fabric's transition to broader production use while tightening how federated and external data is modeled and queried for clarity, performance, and scale control.

changes.name: Data Fabric generally available in Automation Cloud
changes.summary: Data Fabric is now generally available in Automation Cloud.
changes.analysis: This indicates the product is ready for broader production adoption in the cloud environment.
changes.impact: Automation Cloud customers adopting Data Fabric.

changes.name: Entity type selection and mixed local-external entity creation removed
changes.summary: When you create an entity, you now choose its type: Native or Federated. Entities that combine locally stored and external fields can no longer be created, but existing ones continue to work.
changes.analysis: This likely simplifies and clarifies entity modeling boundaries, though it constrains new mixed-source designs.
changes.impact: Users creating new Data Fabric entities; existing mixed entities remain supported.

changes.name: Federated entity can reference native entity
changes.summary: A Federated entity can now reference a native Data Fabric entity as a source.
changes.analysis: This likely increases modeling flexibility by allowing federated designs to build on native Data Fabric data.
changes.impact: Users designing federated entities in Data Fabric.

changes.name: External query behavior changes
changes.summary: Queries over external data now require a filter, return a single page from data warehouse sources, and are limited in result size. Failed queries return clearer errors, and queries run faster.
changes.analysis: The constraints likely aim to improve performance and predictability for external queries, while better errors improve troubleshooting.
changes.impact: Users and integrations querying external data through Data Fabric.

changes.name: Folder-level entities generally available
changes.summary: Folder-level entities and their integration with Automation Solutions are now generally available.
changes.analysis: This likely improves organizational scoping and solution integration for entity usage.
changes.impact: Teams using Data Fabric entities within folders and Automation Solutions.

Document Understanding.summary: Document Understanding updates OCR confidence scoring for handwritten text in the public endpoint and advises threshold recalibration for validation routing. The change affects how confidence-based automation decisions should be tuned.
Document Understanding.overall_analysis: This is significant for customers who rely on OCR confidence thresholds operationally, because scoring now better reflects actual model confidence and may change routing behavior.

changes.name: Handwritten OCR confidence scores adjusted
changes.summary: Confidence scores for handwritten text in the UiPath Document OCR public endpoint now reflect the model's actual confidence. If you route documents to validation on a high OCR confidence threshold, recalibrate the threshold.
changes.analysis: This likely improves score fidelity, but it may alter existing validation-routing outcomes if thresholds were tuned to previous behavior.
changes.impact: Customers using the UiPath Document OCR public endpoint, especially those routing documents based on OCR confidence thresholds.

Functions.summary: Functions adds preview support for JavaScript and TypeScript authoring with HTTP endpoints and identity-aware execution context, plus coding-agent and Autopilot support in Studio Web. The release expands both language options and assisted development.
Functions.overall_analysis: These changes broaden Functions from a capability and developer-experience perspective, making it more attractive for coded extensibility and modern web-oriented function scenarios.

changes.name: JavaScript and TypeScript authoring preview
changes.summary: Functions can now be authored in JavaScript and TypeScript, in preview, with HTTP endpoints and an execution context that carries both the caller's and the function's identities.
changes.analysis: This likely opens Functions to a wider developer audience and enables HTTP-based integration patterns with clearer identity context.
changes.impact: Developers building Functions who prefer JavaScript or TypeScript or need HTTP endpoints.

changes.name: Coded functions via coding agent in public preview
changes.summary: You can now build coded functions with a coding agent, in public preview, through the `uipath-functions` skill.
changes.analysis: This likely accelerates function development by introducing assisted coding workflows.
changes.impact: Developers building coded functions with coding-agent assistance.

changes.name: Autopilot for Function projects in Studio Web
changes.summary: Autopilot is available as a coding agent for Function projects in Studio Web, in public preview. It reads, explains, and reviews source files.
changes.analysis: This likely improves developer productivity for understanding and reviewing function code in Studio Web.
changes.impact: Studio Web users working on Function projects.

Insights.summary: Insights adds public preview coding-agent access to job metrics, failure trends, and process performance queries. This makes analytics data more accessible through agent-based workflows.
Insights.overall_analysis: The release points toward conversational or agent-assisted operational analytics, which may reduce friction in retrieving performance insights.

changes.name: Coding-agent analytics queries in public preview
changes.summary: You can now query job metrics, failure trends, and process performance from a coding agent, in public preview, through the `uipath-insights` skill.
changes.analysis: This likely simplifies access to operational analytics by letting users retrieve insights through coding-agent interactions rather than manual dashboard exploration.
changes.impact: Users and analysts querying operational metrics and process performance through Insights.

Integration Service.summary: Integration Service removes usage metering under certain licensing plans, adds connector availability updates, and includes important migration, deprecation, and removal notices for Perplexity and OpenAI-related activities. The release mixes pricing simplification with potentially disruptive connector changes.
Integration Service.overall_analysis: These changes are operationally significant because they reduce cost constraints for some customers while requiring workflow retesting and migration for affected connectors and deprecated activities.

changes.name: Usage no longer metered or billed under Unified Pricing and Flex
changes.summary: Integration Service usage is no longer metered or billed under the Unified Pricing and Flex licensing plans.
changes.analysis: This likely lowers adoption friction and removes a cost consideration for customers on those plans.
changes.impact: Customers using Integration Service under Unified Pricing and Flex licensing plans.

changes.name: Salesforce Agentforce & Flows connector generally available
changes.summary: The Salesforce Agentforce & Flows connector is now generally available.
changes.analysis: This indicates the connector is ready for broader production use.
changes.impact: Customers integrating with Salesforce Agentforce & Flows.

changes.name: Epic FHIR connector preview
changes.summary: The Epic FHIR connector is available in preview.
changes.analysis: This expands healthcare integration options for customers exploring Epic FHIR scenarios.
changes.impact: Customers interested in Epic FHIR integrations.

changes.name: Perplexity API migration and removals
changes.summary: The Perplexity connector and the GenAI connector's Web Summary activity are migrated to the Perplexity Agent API. Re-test workflows that parse their output. The `r1-1776` model and the List Async Chat activity are no longer available in the Perplexity connector.
changes.analysis: This changes connector behavior and available options, so workflows may need validation or redesign if they depend on prior output formats or removed capabilities.
changes.impact: Users of the Perplexity connector and GenAI connector Web Summary activity, especially workflows parsing returned output or using the removed model or activity.

changes.name: OpenAI Generate Text Completion deprecated
changes.summary: The Generate Text Completion activity in the OpenAI connector is deprecated. After October 23, 2026, workflows that use it fail. Migrate them to Generate Chat Completion.
changes.analysis: This is a time-bound migration requirement for affected workflows, making prompt transition planning necessary.
changes.impact: Users with workflows that use the OpenAI connector's Generate Text Completion activity.

IXP.summary: IXP adds generally available coding-agent support for building IXP projects. The release focuses on assisted development enablement.
IXP.overall_analysis: This extends coding-agent coverage to another product area, likely helping standardize project creation experiences across the platform.

changes.name: IXP projects via coding agent generally available
changes.summary: Building IXP projects with a coding agent is now generally available, through the `uipath-ixp` skill.
changes.analysis: This likely streamlines IXP project development through assisted coding workflows.
changes.impact: Developers building IXP projects.

Maestro.summary: Maestro expands with generally available Maestro Flow and Maestro Automate, adds several preview Flow capabilities, coding-agent support, Studio Desktop solution creation, BPMN Patterns library, and preview Autopilot support across project types. The release significantly broadens Maestro's canvases and development experience.
Maestro.overall_analysis: This is a major platform expansion for Maestro, signaling maturation of orchestration and process design capabilities while unifying low-code, coded, and agent-assisted development across Flow, BPMN, and Case.

changes.name: Maestro Flow generally available
changes.summary: Maestro Flow is now generally available as the third canvas in Maestro Orchestrate, alongside Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) and Case.
changes.analysis: This marks a maturity milestone and formalizes Flow as a core Maestro canvas.
changes.impact: Users of Maestro Orchestrate working with BPMN, Case, and Flow canvases.

changes.name: Maestro Automate generally available
changes.summary: Maestro Automate is now generally available, for short-running workflows of AI agents and APIs on the same canvas and engine as Maestro Flow.
changes.analysis: This likely supports production use of short-running orchestration scenarios that combine agents and APIs in a unified design/runtime model.
changes.impact: Teams orchestrating short-running workflows involving AI agents and APIs in Maestro.

changes.name: Preview Flow capabilities added
changes.summary: Maestro Flow adds several preview capabilities: conversational chat and voice agents, inline Data Fabric entity modeling in VS Code, coded functions as nodes, Autopilot for Flow, and native document processing nodes.
changes.analysis: These previews broaden what Flow can model and execute, especially for conversational, data-aware, and document-centric use cases.
changes.impact: Users exploring advanced or emerging Maestro Flow capabilities.

changes.name: Maestro Flow via coding agent generally available
changes.summary: Building a Maestro Flow with a coding agent is now generally available, through the `uipath-maestro-flow` skill.
changes.analysis: This likely speeds up flow creation and aligns Maestro with the platform's coding-agent strategy.
changes.impact: Developers and designers building Maestro Flow projects.

changes.name: Studio Desktop solution support for Flow projects
changes.summary: You can now create Maestro Flow projects in a Studio Desktop solution, and Flow validation errors appear in the VS Code Problems panel.
changes.analysis: This likely improves desktop-based development workflows and error visibility for Flow authors.
changes.impact: Developers creating Flow projects in Studio Desktop and using VS Code for validation feedback.

changes.name: Patterns library for Maestro BPMN
changes.summary: The Patterns library lets you insert prebuilt, editable process structures into a Maestro BPMN process.
changes.analysis: This likely accelerates process modeling and promotes reuse of common BPMN structures.
changes.impact: Users designing Maestro BPMN processes.

changes.name: Autopilot for Flow, BPMN, and Case in Studio Web preview
changes.summary: Autopilot is available as a coding agent for Maestro Flow, BPMN, and Case projects in Studio Web, in preview.
changes.analysis: This likely improves guided creation and editing across the main Maestro project types in Studio Web.
changes.impact: Studio Web users working on Maestro Flow, BPMN, or Case projects.

Orchestrator.summary: Orchestrator introduces preview Agent Gateway and MCP server capabilities, adds folder-scoped credential stores and environment variables for RPA processes, and changes webhook behavior for bulk queue item insertion. The release enhances agent integration, governance, and process configuration.
Orchestrator.overall_analysis: These updates extend Orchestrator beyond classic orchestration into agent interoperability and configuration management, while also introducing an integration behavior change that webhook consumers should handle carefully.

changes.name: Agent Gateway preview
changes.summary: Agent Gateway is available in preview. It brings the existing MCP Servers area for Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers together with a new A2A Agents area for Agent2Agent (A2A) agents, where you register external agents and expose your conversational agents to A2A clients.
changes.analysis: This likely expands Orchestrator into a hub for agent interoperability, registration, and exposure to external agent ecosystems.
changes.impact: Administrators and developers integrating MCP servers, external agents, and conversational agents through Orchestrator.

changes.name: Platform MCP Servers and Swagger MCP Servers preview
changes.summary: Platform MCP Servers and Swagger MCP Servers are available in preview.
changes.analysis: This likely increases the range of MCP server integrations available through Orchestrator.
changes.impact: Users adopting MCP-based integrations in Orchestrator.

changes.name: Credential stores limited to selected folders
changes.summary: Credential stores can now be limited to selected folders.
changes.analysis: This likely improves security and access control by narrowing where credential stores are available.
changes.impact: Administrators managing credential store scope in Orchestrator folders.

changes.name: Environment variables for RPA processes
changes.summary: You can now configure environment variables for RPA processes. This requires Robot 25.10 or later.
changes.analysis: This likely improves process configurability and deployment flexibility, but it introduces a Robot version prerequisite.
changes.impact: Users configuring RPA processes and robots; requires Robot 25.10 or later.

changes.name: Bulk queue add webhook behavior change
changes.summary: When you add queue items in bulk, Orchestrator may now emit several `queueItem.added` webhook events, each covering a subset of the items.
changes.analysis: Webhook consumers may need to handle multiple events for one bulk operation instead of assuming a single event, affecting downstream processing logic.
changes.impact: Integrations and systems consuming `queueItem.added` webhooks for bulk queue item additions.

products.name: Supply Chain & Retail Solutions: Commercial Pricing
Supply Chain & Retail Solutions: Commercial Pricing, Inventory Management, and Merchandising

Process Mining.summary: Process Mining adds public preview support for building and querying process apps from a coding agent via the `uipath-process-mining` skill.
Process Mining.overall_analysis: This expands agent-assisted interactions with Process Mining by enabling coding-agent-based app creation and querying in preview, which may speed up work for users comfortable with agent-driven workflows while signaling early-stage availability.

changes.name: Coding agent support for process apps
changes.summary: Users can now build and query process apps from a coding agent through the `uipath-process-mining` skill. The capability is in public preview.
changes.analysis: The change likely aims to let users interact with Process Mining programmatically or conversationally through an agent, reducing manual steps for creating and analyzing process apps. Because it is in public preview, adopters should expect the feature to still be maturing.
changes.impact: Affects Process Mining users who want to build or query process apps using a coding agent, especially early adopters evaluating preview features.

Solutions.summary: Solutions now lets users link a resource installed by a previous solution version to an existing resource when changing solution versions or editing deployment configuration.
Solutions.overall_analysis: This adds more flexibility to solution upgrades and deployment configuration, but the stated permanent deletion of the installed resource and its data makes the change operationally significant and potentially risky if not planned carefully.

changes.name: Link previous-version installed resources to existing resources
changes.summary: When changing the solution version or editing a deployment's configuration, users can now link a resource that a previous solution version installed to an existing resource. Linking permanently deletes the installed resource and its data.
changes.analysis: The feature likely helps reuse or remap resources during upgrades or deployment changes instead of keeping duplicate installed resources. However, because linking permanently deletes the installed resource and its data, teams must assess data retention and migration implications before using it.
changes.impact: Affects Solutions users managing version changes and deployment configuration, particularly administrators responsible for resource mapping and data preservation.

Studio Web.summary: Studio Web introduces generally available coding-agent support for building API workflows, new flat-fee pricing for API workflow executions, and public preview Autopilot support as a coding agent for API workflows.
Studio Web.overall_analysis: These changes significantly expand Studio Web's API workflow story by combining broader availability of agent-assisted development with a new execution pricing model and preview automation capabilities for the workflow lifecycle.

changes.name: General availability of coding-agent API workflow building
changes.summary: Building API workflows with a coding agent is now generally available through the `uipath-api-workflow` skill.
changes.analysis: This indicates the capability has moved beyond preview into broader production readiness, making agent-assisted API workflow creation a standard option for Studio Web users.
changes.impact: Affects Studio Web users building API workflows, especially teams looking for production-ready agent-assisted development.

changes.name: Flat-fee pricing for API workflow executions
changes.summary: API workflows are now charged a flat fee per workflow execution, and Integration Service usage inside the workflow is included.
changes.analysis: This changes the commercial model for API workflows and may make costs easier to predict by bundling Integration Service usage within each workflow execution fee.
changes.impact: Affects customers using or planning API workflows in Studio Web, especially budget owners and teams tracking execution and integration costs.

changes.name: Autopilot coding agent for API workflows
changes.summary: Autopilot is available as a coding agent in Studio Web, in public preview. For API workflows, it builds, validates, runs, and publishes workflows.
changes.analysis: The change likely aims to automate more of the API workflow lifecycle inside Studio Web, reducing manual effort from creation through publication. Since it is in public preview, organizations may treat it as an evaluation feature rather than a fully established production capability.
changes.impact: Affects Studio Web users working with API workflows who want agent assistance for building, validation, execution, and publishing.

Supply Chain & Retail Solutions: Commerc.summary: Commercial Pricing now requires 18 data model fields, and related validation failures across Commercial Pricing, Inventory Management, and Merchandising are consolidated into a single email per person with error codes.
Supply Chain & Retail Solutions: Commerc.overall_analysis: The required-field update increases data completeness requirements, while the validation-notification change improves how users receive and interpret validation failures across related supply chain and retail solutions.

changes.name: 18 data model fields now required
changes.summary: In Commercial Pricing, 18 data model fields are now required.
changes.analysis: This likely tightens data-entry or data-model validation requirements to ensure more complete or standardized information for Commercial Pricing processes.
changes.impact: Affects users and implementations of Commercial Pricing that populate or validate the data model, particularly anyone responsible for required field completeness.

changes.name: Consolidated validation failure emails with error codes
changes.summary: For Commercial Pricing, Inventory Management, and Merchandising, a validation run that fails several checks now sends one email to each person, covering every failure they should see, with an error code for each failure.
changes.analysis: This likely reduces notification noise and makes troubleshooting easier by consolidating validation issues into a single message while preserving detail through error codes.
changes.impact: Affects users involved in validation runs and failure triage across Commercial Pricing, Inventory Management, and Merchandising.

Supply Chain & Retail Solutions: Commerc.summary: Validation failures across these supply chain and retail solutions are now consolidated into a single email per person, with all relevant failures and an error code for each one.
Supply Chain & Retail Solutions: Commerc.overall_analysis: This is a usability and operational improvement for validation monitoring, making failure communication more centralized and likely easier to act on across the affected solution areas.

changes.name: Consolidated validation failure emails with error codes
changes.summary: A validation run that fails several checks now sends one email to each person, covering every failure they should see, with an error code for each failure.
changes.analysis: This likely improves clarity and efficiency in handling validation failures by reducing multiple notifications and giving recipients a complete, coded list of issues to review.
changes.impact: Affects recipients of validation failure notifications in Commercial Pricing, Inventory Management, and Merchandising.

products.name: Automation Cloud Administration and Test Cloud Administration
Supply Chain & Retail Solutions: Inventory Management
Supply Chain & Retail Solutions: Commercial Pricing, Inventory Management, and Merchandising

Automation Cloud Administration and Test.summary: The release updates Relay administration, connectivity, client shutdown behavior, and platform API tenant runtime reporting. It also introduces a permission model change for Relay management.
Automation Cloud Administration and Test.overall_analysis: This strengthens delegated administration and expands Relay's integration role for on-premises connectivity, while the permission change may require immediate role updates to preserve access.

changes.name: Dedicated Relay permissions for Relay access
changes.summary: Relay access is now controlled by dedicated Relay permissions instead of administrator group membership, so Tenant Administrators can manage Relay Groups without an Organization Administrator role. Custom roles that granted Relay visibility through the Centralized Access Administration page permission must now include Relay > Relay group > View.
changes.analysis: This shifts Relay administration to a more granular authorization model, reducing dependence on broad administrator roles and enabling more precise access control.
changes.impact: Tenant Administrators, Organization Administrators, and users with custom roles related to Relay administration are affected.

changes.name: TCP-based Relay connections and containerized Relay client support
changes.summary: Relay now supports TCP-based connections to on-premises systems, starting with SAP BAPI, through an on-prem executor. Container deployments of the Relay client using Docker and Podman are supported as of September 10, 2026.
changes.analysis: This broadens Relay's applicability for enterprise connectivity scenarios and makes deployment more flexible for infrastructure teams using containers.
changes.impact: Organizations connecting cloud automation to on-premises systems, especially SAP BAPI environments, and teams deploying Relay clients are affected.

changes.name: Immediate Relay client stop on Relay Group deletion
changes.summary: Deleting a Relay Group now immediately stops all Relay clients connected to it, with no drain period.
changes.analysis: This changes operational behavior for Relay lifecycle management and may require more caution when removing Relay Groups.
changes.impact: Administrators managing Relay Groups and users relying on connected Relay clients are affected.

changes.name: Platform API tenant runtime allocation and usage reporting
changes.summary: The platform API now returns per-tenant robot runtime allocation and usage, and a per-tenant consumption breakdown by process.
changes.analysis: This improves visibility into tenant-level capacity usage and process consumption, supporting monitoring, chargeback, or governance scenarios.
changes.impact: Platform administrators, API consumers, and teams monitoring robot runtime and consumption are affected.

Agents.summary: Agents receives general availability for UiPath Agents in Flow, adds conversational and voice agent flow support, introduces the LLM as Judge guardrail in preview, and makes agent design policies generally available. The updates focus on broader agent-building capability and governance.
Agents.overall_analysis: The release signals maturation of the agent platform by combining production-ready flow-based authoring with new interaction modes and stronger safety and governance controls.

changes.name: UiPath Agents in Flow generally available
changes.summary: UiPath Agents in Flow is now generally available. You configure the agent's system prompt, model, schemas, and tools directly on the Flow canvas, and you can chain multiple agents in a single flow.
changes.analysis: This makes agent construction more accessible and operationally ready, while enabling multi-agent orchestration directly in flows.
changes.impact: Builders creating agent-based automations in Flow are affected.

changes.name: Conversational chat and real-time voice agents in Maestro Flow
changes.summary: You can now build conversational chat agents and real-time voice agents as a Maestro Flow.
changes.analysis: This expands the supported interaction patterns for agents, enabling use cases that require live conversational or voice experiences.
changes.impact: Teams designing customer-facing or interactive agent workflows in Maestro Flow are affected.

changes.name: LLM as Judge guardrail preview
changes.summary: The LLM as Judge guardrail is available in preview. It uses an LLM to evaluate agent prompts, responses, or LLM calls against instructions that you write in natural language.
changes.analysis: This adds a flexible quality and compliance mechanism for agent behavior, potentially improving trust and policy enforcement.
changes.impact: Teams governing, testing, or validating agent behavior are affected.

changes.name: Agent design policies generally available
changes.summary: Agent design policies in the Studio Web governance policy are now generally available.
changes.analysis: This indicates that governance controls for agent design are ready for broader enterprise use.
changes.impact: Administrators and teams enforcing governance over agent design in Studio Web are affected.

Automation Hub.summary: Automation Hub adds Markdown process document upload and preview support, and expands custom-role permissions with view-only access for user administration pages. The changes improve documentation handling and role-based access flexibility.
Automation Hub.overall_analysis: These updates support better process documentation workflows and finer-grained administrative visibility without overprovisioning access.

changes.name: Markdown process document upload and preview
changes.summary: You can now upload Markdown (.md) process documents and preview them in the document viewer.
changes.analysis: This improves compatibility with lightweight documentation formats and may streamline process authoring and review.
changes.impact: Automation Hub users managing process documentation are affected.

changes.name: View-only access for Users and User Roles pages
changes.summary: Custom roles can now be granted view-only access to the Users and User Roles pages.
changes.analysis: This adds more granular role-based access for administrative visibility without edit permissions.
changes.impact: Administrators configuring custom roles and users who need read-only access to user management information are affected.

Automation Ops.summary: Automation Ops expands generally available agent design governance policies and adds new AI Trust Layer policy toggles for Context Grounding and the LLM as Judge guardrail. The release emphasizes governance and control over agent behavior.
Automation Ops.overall_analysis: The release strengthens enterprise policy enforcement for AI agents, helping organizations standardize safety, quality, and execution constraints.

changes.name: Agent design policies generally available with enforcement controls
changes.summary: Agent design policies in the Studio Web governance policy are now generally available. They enforce a minimum agent score, a maximum temperature range, maximum tokens per response, human-in-the-loop escalation, and a maximum number of iterations per agent execution.
changes.analysis: This provides concrete governance levers for controlling agent quality, cost, and operational behavior.
changes.impact: Governance administrators and teams deploying agents through Studio Web are affected.

changes.name: AI Trust Layer policy toggles for Context Grounding and LLM as Judge
changes.summary: The AI Trust Layer policy adds Enable Context Grounding and Enable LLM as Judge guardrail product toggles, both set to Yes by default.
changes.analysis: This gives administrators centralized policy control over two AI safety and quality features, with default enablement encouraging adoption.
changes.impact: Administrators managing AI Trust Layer policies and users subject to those policies are affected.

Data Fabric.summary: Data Fabric introduces preview support for inline entity modeling in VS Code and new Maestro Flow nodes that use those entities without an Integration Service connection. The release links data modeling more directly with flow execution.
Data Fabric.overall_analysis: This reduces friction between defining business entities and using them in automations, suggesting a more integrated low-code data experience.

changes.name: Inline Data Fabric entity modeling in VS Code preview
changes.summary: You can now model Data Fabric entities inline in VS Code, in preview, using a new Data Fabric Entity project type.
changes.analysis: This extends Data Fabric authoring into a developer-centric environment and may improve productivity for users working in VS Code.
changes.impact: Developers and technical users modeling Data Fabric entities in VS Code are affected.

changes.name: New Maestro Flow entity record nodes
changes.summary: Four new Maestro Flow nodes—Query, Create, Update, and Delete entity record—consume these entities without an Integration Service connection.
changes.analysis: This simplifies flow interactions with Data Fabric entities by removing the need for an Integration Service connection in these scenarios.
changes.impact: Users building Maestro Flows that work with Data Fabric entities are affected.

Integration Service.summary: Integration Service adds OAuth 2.0 API access for registered external applications, enhances Connector Builder scripting, expands connector capabilities, updates Azure OpenAI connection input requirements, and improves connector search. The updates span extensibility, authentication, and discoverability.
Integration Service.overall_analysis: This release improves both platform integration depth and connector development flexibility, while also refining usability for authentication and search.

changes.name: OAuth 2.0 access for Integration Service API
changes.summary: You can now call the Integration Service API from a registered external application using OAuth 2.0.
changes.analysis: This enables more standardized and secure external application access to the Integration Service API.
changes.impact: Developers integrating external applications with the Integration Service API are affected.

changes.name: Global Scripts tab in Connector Builder
changes.summary: Connector Builder adds a Global Scripts tab for JavaScript that runs before and after every request a custom connector makes.
changes.analysis: This gives connector builders a reusable mechanism for cross-request logic, reducing duplication and enabling more sophisticated connector behavior.
changes.impact: Developers building custom connectors in Connector Builder are affected.

changes.name: Snowflake and Database Hub connector enhancements
changes.summary: The Snowflake connector adds Microsoft Entra ID authentication, and the Database Hub connector can now connect to Databricks Lakebase.
changes.analysis: These changes broaden supported authentication and target system connectivity for data-related connectors.
changes.impact: Users of the Snowflake connector and Database Hub connector are affected.

changes.name: Coupa connector trigger addition
changes.summary: The Coupa connector adds a Requisition Comment Added trigger.
changes.analysis: This enables automations to react to an additional Coupa event.
changes.impact: Users building event-driven automations with the Coupa connector are affected.

changes.name: Azure OpenAI connection form uses full endpoint URL
changes.summary: The Microsoft Azure OpenAI connection form now takes the full endpoint URL instead of the resource name.
changes.analysis: This changes how connection details are entered and may align configuration more closely with Azure endpoint conventions.
changes.impact: Users configuring Microsoft Azure OpenAI connections are affected.

changes.name: Expanded connector search matching
changes.summary: Connector search now matches tags and descriptions in addition to names.
changes.analysis: This improves discoverability of connectors, especially when users search by capability rather than exact connector name.
changes.impact: Users searching for connectors in Integration Service are affected.

IXP.summary: IXP adds preview support for bring your own subscription for certain projects and keeps United Kingdom Gemini 2.5 Flash requests within the United Kingdom region. The changes focus on cost flexibility and data locality.
IXP.overall_analysis: The release improves deployment control for AI-powered document processing by offering customer-managed model subscriptions and stronger regional routing behavior.

changes.name: Bring your own subscription preview
changes.summary: Bring your own subscription (BYOS) is available in preview, letting Unstructured and Complex Documents projects run on your own Gemini or GPT subscriptions, with discounted consumption rates for projects that run entirely on them.
changes.analysis: This gives customers more control over model usage and cost structure, especially when they already maintain provider subscriptions.
changes.impact: Customers running Unstructured and Complex Documents projects with Gemini or GPT models are affected.

changes.name: United Kingdom regional routing for Gemini 2.5 Flash
changes.summary: Requests from the United Kingdom region for the Gemini 2.5 Flash model now stay in the United Kingdom.
changes.analysis: This strengthens regional processing behavior, which may support residency, latency, or compliance objectives.
changes.impact: Customers in the United Kingdom region using the Gemini 2.5 Flash model are affected.

Maestro.summary: Maestro introduces preview evaluations for BPMN, expands Maestro Case with preview AI-assisted orchestration and case building, enhances Autonomous Agent node tool controls, and extends the v3 CaseApp API. The release deepens orchestration, evaluation, and case management capabilities.
Maestro.overall_analysis: These changes advance Maestro as a more intelligent orchestration platform, combining evaluation tooling, agent-assisted case handling, and more flexible API and tool integration support.

changes.name: Maestro BPMN evaluations preview
changes.summary: Evaluations for Maestro BPMN are available in preview, letting you group expected outcomes into evaluation sets and score each run with deterministic or LLM-judge evaluators.
changes.analysis: This adds a structured way to assess process execution quality and correctness, supporting testing and optimization.
changes.impact: Users designing and validating Maestro BPMN workflows are affected.

changes.name: Maestro Case preview enhancements
changes.summary: In Maestro Case, the Case Manager Agent (preview) can make orchestration decisions for events that your deterministic rules don't cover, and you can build a case with a coding agent of your choice (preview).
changes.analysis: This introduces more adaptive case orchestration and flexible case-building assistance where static rules are insufficient.
changes.impact: Users building and managing cases in Maestro Case are affected.

changes.name: Autonomous Agent node MCP controls and schema refresh
changes.summary: Maestro Flow Autonomous Agent nodes gain richer MCP tool controls and a Refresh schema before call toggle that keeps tool schemas up to date.
changes.analysis: This improves control and reliability when agent nodes interact with tools whose schemas may change.
changes.impact: Users configuring Autonomous Agent nodes in Maestro Flow are affected.

changes.name: v3 CaseApp API endpoint additions
changes.summary: The v3 CaseApp API adds endpoints to close a case instance and to trigger ad hoc tasks, with an optional taskInput payload.
changes.analysis: This expands programmatic case lifecycle and task management capabilities for integrations.
changes.impact: Developers and integrators using the v3 CaseApp API are affected.

Orchestrator.summary: Orchestrator adds AWS Secrets Manager integration through Integration Service, updates Credentials Proxy 2.2.2 with .NET and Delinea support, and enhances several registry pages with grouping and metadata columns. The release improves secrets management and operational usability.
Orchestrator.overall_analysis: This strengthens enterprise credential-store integration and modernizes related infrastructure, while also making resource and deployment views easier to organize and inspect.

changes.name: AWS Secrets Manager credential store integration
changes.summary: AWS Secrets Manager can now be integrated as a credential store through an Integration Service connection, which supports IAM role-based authentication.
changes.analysis: This expands supported secrets back ends and aligns Orchestrator with cloud-native AWS credential management practices.
changes.impact: Administrators configuring credential stores in AWS-backed environments are affected.

changes.name: Orchestrator Credentials Proxy 2.2.2 update
changes.summary: Orchestrator Credentials Proxy 2.2.2 updates the framework to .NET 10.0.11 and adds Delinea Secret Server as a read-only credential store. Install the .NET 10 Hosting Bundle before you upgrade.
changes.analysis: This update adds another enterprise credential store option and introduces a technical upgrade prerequisite that administrators must plan for.
changes.impact: Administrators upgrading Orchestrator Credentials Proxy and using external credential stores are affected.

changes.name: Registry page grouping and metadata columns
changes.summary: The Solution deployments, Processes, and Resources registry pages add a Group by option, and the Resources and Processes pages add Labels and Properties columns.
changes.analysis: This improves organization and visibility in registry views, which may help users manage larger environments more efficiently.
changes.impact: Users managing solution deployments, processes, and resources in Orchestrator are affected.

Studio Web.summary: Studio Web adds nested folders for solution project organization and speeds up local debugging by uploading only changed files. The updates improve project structure and developer iteration time.
Studio Web.overall_analysis: These enhancements target everyday productivity by making complex solutions easier to organize and reducing local debug overhead.

changes.name: Nested folders in Solution Explorer
changes.summary: You can now organize the projects in a solution into nested folders from the Solution Explorer.
changes.analysis: This improves manageability for larger or more complex solutions.
changes.impact: Studio Web users organizing multi-project solutions are affected.

changes.name: Incremental file upload for local debug sessions
changes.summary: Local debug sessions now upload only the files that changed since the last session, so they start faster.
changes.analysis: This reduces debugging startup time and improves the edit-test cycle.
changes.impact: Studio Web users running local debug sessions are affected.

Test Manager.summary: Test Manager adds controlled-availability Playwright test automation for eligible Test Cloud tenants, expands Integration Service connector activities, and improves requirement and execution log experiences. The changes strengthen test execution integration and usability.
Test Manager.overall_analysis: This release broadens testing ecosystem compatibility and improves both automation connectivity and day-to-day test management workflows.

changes.name: Playwright test automation controlled availability
changes.summary: Playwright test automation is available in controlled availability to eligible tenants, letting Test Manager run test cases backed by existing Playwright suites (Test Cloud delivery only).
changes.analysis: This extends Test Manager to a widely used external testing framework while limiting rollout to eligible tenants.
changes.impact: Eligible Test Cloud tenants using or considering Playwright-based test suites are affected.

changes.name: UiPath Test Manager connector activity expansion
changes.summary: The UiPath Test Manager connector in Integration Service adds seven activities, including Create Test Step, Get Requirements, and Get Test Cases.
changes.analysis: This expands integration and automation possibilities for Test Manager operations.
changes.impact: Users automating Test Manager workflows through Integration Service are affected.

changes.name: Requirement details and execution log UI improvements
changes.summary: The requirement details page is redesigned, and the Logs tab of a test execution adds a full-message pop-up with a Copy message button, message search, and a Level filter.
changes.analysis: These usability enhancements make requirement review and log inspection more effective.
changes.impact: Test Manager users reviewing requirements and investigating test execution logs are affected.

Supply Chain & Retail Solutions: Invento.summary: Inventory Management changes foreign-key handling so rows with unresolved references are retained and flagged, with asynchronous validation clearing the flag later when parent rows arrive. This removes the need to ingest parent tables before child tables.
Supply Chain & Retail Solutions: Invento.overall_analysis: The update makes ingestion workflows more resilient and less order-dependent, reducing operational friction in data loading pipelines.

changes.name: Retain and asynchronously validate unresolved foreign-key rows
changes.summary: Rows whose only problem is an unresolved foreign-key reference are now kept in the destination table and flagged, and a new async_foreign_key validation clears the flag once the parent row is loaded, so tables no longer have to be ingested parent-before-child.
changes.analysis: This reduces failed or blocked loads caused solely by ingestion order and supports more flexible data pipeline sequencing.
changes.impact: Teams loading data into Inventory Management destination tables and monitoring data validation are affected.

Supply Chain & Retail Solutions: Commerc.summary: Foreign-key checks now surface in the Data Quality Dashboard through two new panels. The change improves visibility into validation issues and asynchronous foreign-key processing.
Supply Chain & Retail Solutions: Commerc.overall_analysis: This enhances monitoring and diagnostics for data quality by exposing foreign-key validation outcomes directly in the dashboard.

changes.name: Foreign-key reporting in Data Quality Dashboard
changes.summary: Foreign-key checks now report to the Data Quality Dashboard, with a new FK validation issue rows panel and an Async foreign-key checks panel.
changes.analysis: This gives users clearer operational insight into foreign-key data quality problems and async validation activity.
changes.impact: Users monitoring data quality in Commercial Pricing, Inventory Management, and Merchandising are affected.

products.name: Automation Cloud Public Sector Administration and Test Cloud Public Sector Administration

Automation Cloud Public Sector Administr.summary: Administration now lets users open consumption charts directly from each unit card on the Consumables tab through a new Overview button, without opening the full Consumables Center dashboard.
Automation Cloud Public Sector Administr.overall_analysis: This change appears to streamline access to consumption insights and reduce navigation steps for administrators monitoring usage.

changes.name: Overview button on Consumables unit cards
changes.summary: Each unit card on the Consumables tab now includes an Overview button that displays consumption charts without opening the full Consumables Center dashboard.
changes.analysis: This likely improves efficiency for administrators who need quick visibility into consumption data by surfacing charts in place instead of requiring a full dashboard transition.
changes.impact: Users of Automation Cloud Public Sector Administration and Test Cloud Public Sector Administration who monitor consumables usage on the Consumables tab.

Integration Service.summary: Integration Service adds general availability for the Salesforce Agentforce & Flows connector, migrates the GenAI connector's Web Summary activity to the Perplexity Agent API, and deprecates the OpenAI connector's Generate Text Completion activity with workflow failures after October 23, 2026.
Integration Service.overall_analysis: These changes expand production-ready connector availability, introduce behavior-affecting backend changes that require workflow retesting, and announce a time-bound deprecation that requires migration to avoid failures. Overall, the release combines feature maturation with important maintenance actions for existing automations.

changes.name: Salesforce Agentforce & Flows connector generally available
changes.summary: The Salesforce Agentforce & Flows connector is now generally available.
changes.analysis: General availability indicates the connector is ready for broader production use and may give customers more confidence to adopt it in live integrations.
changes.impact: Teams using or planning to use Integration Service with Salesforce Agentforce & Flows.

changes.name: Web Summary activity migrated to Perplexity Agent API
changes.summary: The GenAI connector's Web Summary activity is migrated to the Perplexity Agent API, and workflows that parse its output should be re-tested.
changes.analysis: Because the underlying API changed, output format or behavior may differ, so workflows that depend on parsed results could require validation or adjustment.
changes.impact: Users of the GenAI connector's Web Summary activity, especially workflows that parse the activity output.

changes.name: Generate Text Completion deprecated in OpenAI connector
changes.summary: The Generate Text Completion activity in the OpenAI connector is deprecated. After October 23, 2026, workflows that use it fail, and users should migrate to Generate Chat Completion.
changes.analysis: This is a time-sensitive deprecation with an explicit failure date, making migration necessary to maintain workflow continuity. It signals a shift toward the newer Generate Chat Completion activity as the supported path.
changes.impact: Users with workflows that currently use the OpenAI connector's Generate Text Completion activity.

products.name: Automation Cloud Public Sector Administration and Test Cloud Public Sector Administration

Automation Cloud Public Sector Administr.summary: Microsoft Entra ID directory integration now supports delegated and app-only access and cached user tokens for group membership checks. This extends group membership evaluation to unattended automations and service-to-service scenarios.
Automation Cloud Public Sector Administr.overall_analysis: This expands identity integration coverage beyond interactive user scenarios, which likely improves access evaluation for automated and service-driven workloads in public sector cloud environments.

changes.name: Expanded Microsoft Entra ID directory integration scopes and token handling
changes.summary: The Microsoft Entra ID directory integration now supports the Delegated and app-only access scope and the Use cached user tokens for group membership checks option, extending group membership evaluation to unattended automations and service-to-service scenarios.
changes.analysis: The change appears intended to support more authentication patterns and make directory-based group evaluation usable in non-interactive contexts such as unattended automations and service-to-service integrations.
changes.impact: Organizations using Microsoft Entra ID directory integration in Automation Cloud Public Sector Administration or Test Cloud Public Sector Administration, especially those running unattended automations or service-to-service scenarios.

Integration Service.summary: Integration Service adds OAuth 2.0 access for registered external applications through its API and expands connector capabilities across Snowflake, Database Hub, Coupa, and Microsoft Azure OpenAI. These updates improve authentication options and broaden supported integration scenarios.
Integration Service.overall_analysis: The release strengthens Integration Service as an extensibility and connectivity layer by enabling external app API access and enhancing several connectors with new authentication methods, targets, triggers, and configuration behavior.

changes.name: OAuth 2.0 support for Integration Service API
changes.summary: You can now call the Integration Service API from a registered external application using OAuth 2.0.
changes.analysis: This likely enables more secure and standardized API access for external applications, making it easier to integrate Integration Service into enterprise app ecosystems.
changes.impact: Developers and organizations integrating registered external applications with the Integration Service API.

changes.name: Snowflake connector adds Microsoft Entra ID authentication
changes.summary: The Snowflake connector now supports Microsoft Entra ID authentication.
changes.analysis: This likely gives customers an additional enterprise authentication method for Snowflake connections, aligning connector access with identity management practices based on Microsoft Entra ID.
changes.impact: Users configuring the Snowflake connector, especially organizations standardizing on Microsoft Entra ID authentication.

changes.name: Database Hub connector supports Databricks Lakebase
changes.summary: The Database Hub connector can now connect to Databricks Lakebase.
changes.analysis: This broadens the range of supported data platforms and likely makes Database Hub more useful for organizations working with Databricks Lakebase environments.
changes.impact: Users of the Database Hub connector who need connectivity to Databricks Lakebase.

changes.name: Coupa connector adds Requisition Comment Added trigger
changes.summary: The Coupa connector adds a Requisition Comment Added trigger.
changes.analysis: This likely enables new event-driven automation scenarios based on comments being added to requisitions in Coupa.
changes.impact: Users building automations or integrations with the Coupa connector.

changes.name: Microsoft Azure OpenAI connection form uses full endpoint URL
changes.summary: The Microsoft Azure OpenAI connection form now takes the full endpoint URL instead of the resource name.
changes.analysis: This likely changes connection setup to use a more explicit endpoint value, which may support broader or clearer configuration patterns for Azure OpenAI connections.
changes.impact: Users configuring Microsoft Azure OpenAI connections in Integration Service.

Test Manager.summary: Test Manager updates the requirement details page, enhances test execution logs with richer inspection and filtering tools, and adds an optional Clipboard data argument to MCP tools for adding and updating test steps. These changes improve usability in both the interface and tooling.
Test Manager.overall_analysis: The release focuses on productivity and diagnostics in Test Manager by improving page design, making execution logs easier to inspect, and extending MCP tooling inputs for test step management.

changes.name: Requirement details page redesign
changes.summary: The requirement details page is redesigned.
changes.analysis: The redesign likely aims to improve usability, readability, or workflow efficiency when reviewing and managing requirement details.
changes.impact: Test Manager users working with requirement details.

changes.name: Enhanced test execution Logs tab
changes.summary: The Logs tab of a test execution now includes a full-message pop-up with a Copy message button, message search, and a Level filter.
changes.analysis: These additions likely make troubleshooting and log review faster by improving visibility into full messages and adding search and filtering capabilities.
changes.impact: Test Manager users reviewing test execution logs, especially those diagnosing failures or investigating execution behavior.

changes.name: Clipboard data argument for MCP test step tools
changes.summary: The Test Manager MCP tools for adding and updating test steps now accept an optional Clipboard data argument.
changes.analysis: This likely streamlines test step creation and updates in MCP-based workflows by allowing supplementary clipboard content to be passed into the tools.
changes.impact: Users of Test Manager MCP tools for adding and updating test steps.

Apps.summary: Apps now supports Coded Apps and Coded Action Apps in Automation Cloud Dedicated and Test Cloud Dedicated. Coded Action Apps have minimum SDK version requirements.
Apps.overall_analysis: This expands development options for Apps by enabling code-based app experiences in these cloud environments, but adoption depends on using the required SDK versions.

changes.name: Coded Apps and Coded Action Apps availability
changes.summary: Coded Apps and Coded Action Apps are now available in Automation Cloud Dedicated and Test Cloud Dedicated. Coded Action Apps require `uipath-typescript` SDK 1.7.1 or later and `@uipath/coded-action-app` SDK 1.0.0 or later.
changes.analysis: This likely enables developers to build more customizable app experiences using code in dedicated cloud environments. The stated SDK requirements indicate teams may need to update their development dependencies before using Coded Action Apps.
changes.impact: Developers building apps in Automation Cloud Dedicated and Test Cloud Dedicated, especially those using or planning to use Coded Action Apps.

Studio Web.summary: Studio Web introduces workflow authoring and deployment usability improvements, including a new default Deploy action, nested solution folders, generally available coding-agent support for API workflows, and faster local debug sessions. These changes span both the September 17 and September 24 releases.
Studio Web.overall_analysis: The updates suggest a focus on improving developer productivity and organization in Studio Web. They streamline deployment, improve project structure management, expand AI-assisted API workflow creation, and reduce debug iteration time.

changes.name: Deploy as default toolbar action
changes.summary: **Deploy** is now the default toolbar button for packaging and deploying a solution, while **Publish** is available from the **Deploy** dropdown.
changes.analysis: This likely simplifies the primary release workflow by emphasizing deployment as the main action in the toolbar. Users accustomed to Publish as a primary action may need to adjust to the updated interface flow.
changes.impact: Studio Web users who package and deploy solutions from the toolbar.

changes.name: Nested folders in Solution Explorer
changes.summary: Projects in a solution can now be organized into nested folders from the **Solution Explorer**.
changes.analysis: This likely improves manageability for larger or more complex solutions by allowing clearer project organization. It can help teams structure multi-project solutions more effectively.
changes.impact: Studio Web users managing solutions with multiple projects.

changes.name: API workflows with coding agent generally available
changes.summary: Building API workflows with a coding agent is now generally available through the `uipath-api-workflow` skill.
changes.analysis: General availability indicates the feature is ready for broader production use. This likely helps users create API workflows more efficiently with coding-agent assistance.
changes.impact: Studio Web users building API workflows, particularly those adopting coding-agent-assisted development.

changes.name: Faster local debug uploads
changes.summary: Local debug sessions now upload only the files that changed since the last session, allowing sessions to start faster.
changes.analysis: This likely reduces waiting time during iterative development by minimizing upload volume between debug runs. The improvement is especially useful for frequent testing cycles.
changes.impact: Studio Web users running local debug sessions.

Test Manager.summary: Test Manager updates improve requirement and execution log usability, and expand MCP tool inputs for test-step management. The changes focus on better test review and more flexible test authoring workflows.
Test Manager.overall_analysis: These enhancements appear aimed at improving tester efficiency and usability in both the interface and automation tooling. Better log inspection and optional clipboard-based input can support faster troubleshooting and test maintenance.

changes.name: Requirement details and test execution logs enhancements
changes.summary: The requirement details page is redesigned, and the **Logs** tab of a test execution now includes a full-message pop-up with a **Copy message** button, message search, and a **Level** filter.
changes.analysis: This likely improves usability when reviewing requirements and diagnosing test execution issues. More detailed log interaction can help users inspect and filter execution information more efficiently.
changes.impact: Test Manager users reviewing requirements and investigating test execution logs.

changes.name: Clipboard data support in MCP tools
changes.summary: The Test Manager MCP tools for adding and updating test steps now accept an optional **Clipboard data** argument.
changes.analysis: This likely makes MCP-based test-step creation and updates more flexible by allowing additional input content to be passed directly. It may streamline workflows that involve copying step content from another source.
changes.impact: Users of Test Manager MCP tools who add or update test steps programmatically or through assisted tooling.

Solutions.summary: Solutions now lets users link a resource installed by a previous solution version to an existing resource during version changes or deployment configuration edits. The operation permanently deletes the installed resource and its data.
Solutions.overall_analysis: This adds flexibility when reconciling resources across solution versions or deployment changes, but it also introduces a clearly destructive action. Users need to evaluate data retention carefully before using it.

changes.name: Link previously installed resource to existing resource
changes.summary: When changing the solution version or editing a deployment's configuration, you can now link a resource that a previous solution version installed to an existing resource. Linking permanently deletes the installed resource and its data.
changes.analysis: This likely helps align deployments with resources that already exist instead of keeping duplicate installed resources. Because the release notes explicitly state that linking permanently deletes the installed resource and its data, users must handle this action carefully to avoid unintended data loss.
changes.impact: Solutions users updating solution versions or editing deployment configurations where previously installed resources are being reconciled with existing resources.

products.name: Automation Cloud Dedicated Admin / Test Cloud Dedicated Admin

Automation Cloud Dedicated Admin / Test.summary: The admin experience adds a Check access API enhancement that returns effective access across the organization, including tenant-level assignments from all active tenants. This expands visibility into permissions for users, groups, and external applications.
Automation Cloud Dedicated Admin / Test.overall_analysis: This update appears aimed at improving organization-wide access auditing and permission verification in dedicated cloud environments. It likely helps administrators investigate and validate access more efficiently across tenants from a single API capability.

changes.name: Check access API returns organization-wide effective access
changes.summary: Organization Administrators can now use the Check access API to retrieve effective access for a user, group, or external application across the organization, including tenant-level assignments from every active tenant.
changes.analysis: The likely purpose is to centralize and simplify access reviews by exposing effective permissions across the full organization scope, rather than requiring separate tenant-by-tenant checks.
changes.impact: Organization Administrators managing users, groups, external applications, and tenant-level access assignments across active tenants are affected.

Orchestrator.summary: Orchestrator adds broader package source support, queue monitoring enhancements, and job execution and recording controls. It also improves job troubleshooting by exposing stop reasons in the Job state history timeline.
Orchestrator.overall_analysis: These changes collectively suggest a focus on operational flexibility, observability, and execution control. They likely benefit administrators and operators who manage package sources, monitor queue health, and troubleshoot or govern job execution behavior.

changes.name: Support for multiple package sources per category
changes.summary: Orchestrator now supports multiple NuGet feeds, npm registries, and PyPI indexes instead of a single feed per category.
changes.analysis: This likely increases deployment flexibility for teams that consume packages from multiple internal or external repositories across different package ecosystems.
changes.impact: Administrators and development or operations teams configuring package sources for NuGet, npm, and PyPI in Orchestrator are affected.

changes.name: Queue monitoring and Start job dialog improvements
changes.summary: The per-queue monitoring dashboard adds a Queue item failures by reason widget, and the Start job dialog lets you pin the Execution settings panel open.
changes.analysis: The new monitoring widget likely helps identify recurring failure patterns faster, while the dialog change improves usability for users who frequently adjust execution settings.
changes.impact: Users monitoring queue performance and users manually starting jobs in Orchestrator are affected.

changes.name: Maximum job recording duration and stop-reason visibility
changes.summary: You can set the maximum job recording duration, up to 15 minutes on the Enterprise plan (Unified Pricing) or the Advanced plan (Flex), and the Job state history timeline now shows why a job was stopped.
changes.analysis: This likely gives organizations more control over recording resource usage and auditing while improving troubleshooting by exposing explicit stop reasons in job history.
changes.impact: Administrators configuring job recording and operators reviewing stopped jobs are affected, especially on Enterprise plan (Unified Pricing) and Advanced plan (Flex).

Studio Web.summary: Studio Web introduces read-only access for solutions and adds notifications when solutions are shared. These updates improve collaboration while limiting unintended edits.
Studio Web.overall_analysis: The broader significance is improved governance and collaboration around solution sharing. Read-only access likely supports review workflows, while notifications help recipients discover shared content promptly.

changes.name: Read-only solution access and sharing
changes.summary: You can now open a solution in read-only mode and share a solution with read-only access without granting edit permissions.
changes.analysis: This likely enables safer collaboration scenarios such as review, approval, or stakeholder visibility without risking unwanted modifications.
changes.impact: Solution owners, collaborators, and reviewers using Studio Web are affected.

changes.name: Notifications for shared solutions
changes.summary: You now receive a notification when someone shares a solution with you.
changes.analysis: This likely improves discoverability and responsiveness in collaboration workflows by making sharing events more visible.
changes.impact: Users who receive shared solutions in Studio Web are affected.

Test Manager.summary: Test Manager improves manual execution context and export behavior, and it removes the iText PDF library dependency with resulting limitations for PDF attachment handling in the cloud. The PDF-related change introduces reduced functionality and is explicitly a breaking change.
Test Manager.overall_analysis: These updates combine usability improvements with a significant dependency-driven change in document handling. The breaking change likely affects teams that relied on PDF image extraction or richer PDF attachment reading in cloud-based testing workflows.

changes.name: Manual execution assistant and asynchronous Excel export enhancements
changes.summary: The manual execution assistant now shows the test case description above Precondition, and Excel export of requirements and test cases is now asynchronous with one column per custom field.
changes.analysis: These changes likely improve test execution clarity and make large or structured exports more usable and less disruptive by processing them asynchronously and preserving custom-field separation.
changes.impact: Manual testers and users exporting requirements and test cases from Test Manager are affected.

changes.name: Removal of iText PDF library dependency
changes.summary: The iText PDF library dependency was removed: reading PDF attachments in the cloud is now text-only, and image extraction from PDF attachments is no longer supported.
changes.analysis: The likely purpose is dependency removal, but the practical impact is reduced PDF processing capability in cloud scenarios. Teams that depended on image extraction or richer PDF attachment reading may need to adjust their workflows.
changes.impact: Cloud users of Test Manager who read PDF attachments or rely on image extraction from PDF attachments are affected.
